'''Tjupan''' (Tjupany) is one of the [[Wati languages]] of the large [[Pama–Nyungan languages|Pama–Nyungan family]] of Australia. It is sometimes counted as a dialect of the [[Western Desert Language]], but is classified as a distinct language by Bowern.<ref>Claire Bowern and Quentin Atkinson. 2012. Computational phylogenetics and the internal structure of Pama-Nyungan. Language 88. 817-845. Johns Hopkins University Press.</ref>

The spelling "Tjupan" follows the [[Goldfields Language Centre]] and is used for a small dictionary published by the [[Ngalia Heritage Research Council]]. "Madoidja" (Madoitja) is a location name.

Extinct Birniridjara ("Pini") was close geographically and was reported to be [[Mutual intelligibility|mutually intelligible]], but is undocumented and it is not known if it was closer to Tjupan than to other Western Desert languages.

Tjupan is classed as a highly [[Endangered language|endangered]] language, with only 6 fully fluent speakers remaining.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wangka.com.au/tjupan-3|title=Tjupan, Goldfields Aboriginal Language Centre|website=www.wangka.com.au|access-date=2021-11-26}}</ref>
